rows.notes: Lean/EventAlgebra/LuedersPhaseInstrument.lean constructs a declared Lüders instrument on the committed eight-context effect table and proves the channel clauses as exact finite matrix algebra: each outcome map X ↦ E X E is completely positive through a singleton Kraus family and trace-nonincreasing on positive-semidefinite inputs, the summed channel of each context is trace preserving on every matrix and hence CPTP, and the induced effects equal the committed table with the declared Pauli-Y projector in the phase slot. The normalized post-measurement state is certain of its effect, a state-update proxy for readback. SourcePhaseInstrumentOutcomeBridge proves that all 48 enabled entries of the generated source phase relation agree with the corresponding normalized outcome of this declared instrument. SourcePhaseCommonPreparationHull evaluates those declared outcome maps on every common-support source state and proves an exact convex-hull compatibility with the declared run state. The run state is outside the generated state domain, no generated source step starts there, and a generated result loses all-event support; the hull therefore supplies neither a source implementation nor a sequential instrument protocol. Its generated outcome index is semantic, not a recorded public outcome. The clause that outcome readback agrees with a recorded public outcome is open: no public outcome is typed. The effect table alone does not determine the instrument, and the committed repeatability clause is strictly weaker than selection. InstrumentSelectionByCertainStates proves a sharper conditional result: among finite Kraus-form maps with the committed projective effects, declared certain-state invariance is equivalent to the Lüders maps. That operational invariance remains a declared hypothesis and is not source-implemented; no recorded public outcome is bound. Removal therefore still needs a source-facing instrument whose readback is bound to public outcomes under PR-65. SourceBoundInstrumentInterface identifies induced effects with the static outcome-map trace/expected-frequency surface and proves the determined interface does not pin the instrument; a recorded public outcome is not typed in the corpus, so the readback clause of this row stays open. The INS-03 v2 replay gate adds executable transcript verification against a proposed generation semantics; every verdict is explicitly unauthenticated and no instrument realization follows, so this premise stays open.

rows.name: source-produced phase preparation and readback provenance
rows.statement: One source construction supplies the common preparation used across the phase and real contexts, selects the phase-sensitive effect or instrument, produces the public outcomes through that instrument, and binds preparation, context, operation, readback, and receipt custody to one run. Deterministic recomputation of Born weights from declared matrices does not supply this provenance.
rows.notes: Removal needs a common source-produced preparation, an oriented effect or orientation-invariant binary context, a selected instrument, recorded public outcomes, and an authenticated producer/run/custody receipt. The Lueders instrument and source-transition bridge are exact compatibility mathematics only. InstrumentSelectionByCertainStates conditionally selects the Lueders maps from projective effects plus declared certain-state invariance, but it neither derives that invariance from the source nor selects the events, preparation, producer, readback, or custody. The source-phase enumeration conditionally yields unordered {+Y,-Y} under a declared adapter; it does not source-select +Y. The convex hull is retrospective and supplies no mixing or sequential protocol. SourceBoundInstrumentInterface's determined table is an expected-frequency surface, not public readback, while its inhabited Prop fields and natural-number digest are freely stipulable placeholders, not a proof that custody is external. INS-03 v1 is now explicitly static-only: it checks exact fixture conformance and correct 0<=E<=I bounds, emits STATIC_COMMITTED_FIXTURE_CONFORMANT, and rejects every producer claim because authentication is unimplemented. A viable v2 must bind raw producer artifacts, identity, run configuration, outcomes, and cryptographic custody independently. PR-65 stays open. The v2 authenticated-binding specification names the owner-key custody half exactly and the replay verifier fail-closes every producer claim; no source production, run, or custody exists, so this premise stays open.

rows.name: declared discrete kinetic term of the temporal Maxwell action
rows.statement: The temporal Maxwell packet is the Euler-Lagrange system of one declared discrete action on a finite step window: the committed local sourced face action at the forward step, with its committed seam-current coupling, plus the declared kinetic term (h/2)|E_n|^2 with E_n = -(A_{n+1}-A_n)/h - d phi_n, plus the port-load coupling h <rho_n, phi_n>. Stationarity under endpoint-vanishing variations of A is equivalent to the step-scaled Ampere update E_{n+1}-E_n = h (C^T B_{n+1} - J_n) at every interior step, and stationarity under variations of phi is equivalent to the Gauss constraint at every window step. The kinetic term and the step h are the declared inputs; the unit-step recurrence of the earlier packet is the h = 1 instance and is no separate declaration.
rows.notes: The staggered form (1/2)|E_n|^2 + (1/2)<B_n, B_{n+1}> is exactly conserved for zero current and is nonnegative under h^2 Lambda <= 4 for any Courant constant Lambda with |C v|^2 <= Lambda |v|^2; for h^2 Lambda < 4 the electric and magnetic energies are bounded at every step by 8 E_0/(4 - h^2 Lambda) and 16 E_0/(4 - h^2 Lambda). On the committed carrier the sharp constant Lambda = 3 + sqrt(5) is proved by explicit rational spectral projectors of C C^T; an explicit eigenvector of C^T C for 3 + sqrt(5) gives an unbounded zero-current solution whenever h^2 (3 + sqrt(5)) > 4, and an explicit integer eigenvector for 5 gives one whenever 5 h^2 > 4, so the declared unit step h = 1 is unstable. Removal of this row needs a derivation of the kinetic term from the three OPH axioms or from repair dynamics; physical time, calibration, and comparison stay under PR-15 and PR-53. CertifiedScaledStepInstrument consumes the declared kinetic-term step layer at the committed selection h = 4/5 with a rational margin certificate; the kinetic term itself stays declared.

rows.statement: The finite electroweak composition uses one declared complex doublet with q=6Y equal to three, a four-parameter weak-hypercharge infinitesimal action with declared positive couplings, and the displayed finite normalization. This is a mathematical grammar declaration, not selection of a physical scalar field or kinetic action.

rows.statement: The finite composition declares lambda>0, a model-shell radius r>0, the potential lambda times (normSq(h)-r^2)^2, and the chosen point (0,r). Its minimizer, stabilizer, quadratic-coefficient, and gauge-mass-form identities are conditional finite consequences of this packet.
rows.notes: The Lean parameter called vev is the finite model-shell radius. If the vector is identified with the conventional Standard Model form (0,v_SM/sqrt(2)), then r=v_SM/sqrt(2); translating the finite mass-form coefficient to a physical mass additionally needs PR-48 kinetic normalization and PR-49 physical vacuum/scale attachment.

rows.statement: The finite electroweak composition selects one epsilon-paired doublet-singlet Yukawa line with one declared real coefficient y and proves its exact bilinear value at the declared finite vacuum. It supplies no family matrices, physical chiral attachment, texture, phase, or measured mass identification.

rows.statement: The physical position action of the compared regime is homogeneous, its sole direct support is the complete thirty-direction edge orbit of the committed seam current, and its source weights are equal across the thirty directions. The committed corpus proves the control counterpart only: the seam-derived control symbol has complete edge support with one common squared chord and equal control weight (source_seam_edge30_control_certificate), and no committed theorem attaches that control symbol to a physical action.

The current interface fields are inhabited Prop placeholders; propext shows only that this schema carries no data-level witness, not that every future source construction is impossible.

rows.statement: The compared observable lives in a continuous field sector, and the comparison reads the same operator sector that the committed source theorem fixes for the seam-derived symbol. No committed theorem selects the physical sector or identifies the committed symbol with a laboratory operator.

rows.notes: Declared choice recorded as declared. The current ratio and permissive-schema theorems prove only that those inputs do not select a scale; they are not a universal no-go. A later independent source-scale theorem would convert this row to disposition remove. No scale number is proposed here.

rows.statement: One coherent frame carries the comparison, and a boost transport connects that frame to the source frame of the committed symbol, so that the intrinsic coefficients are read in a resolved frame. No committed theorem supplies frame resolution or boost transport for the FZ-12 comparison path.

rows.statement: The readout of any eligible comparison isolates nuisance parameters and calibrates joint coverage under rules fixed before exposure, as the frozen decision rule requires for every verdict class. These are declared analysis conventions of the comparison protocol, not source-derivable structure.
rows.notes: Declared choice recorded as declared. The current Prop field merely names the slot and supplies no nuisance or coverage rule content. A future freeze must bind concrete preregistered rules and artifacts.

rows.statement: A pre-exposure same-action, same-sector source theorem fixes a positive lower bound a_min for the admissible scales in the comparison units, and the preregistered sensitivity and remainder contract covers every admissible scale at or above a_min. Independent source invariants remain viable; the current numeric and Prop placeholders do not block them.

rows.name: pathwise weak fairness for canonical adaptive repair
rows.statement: Along one canonical adaptive repair run, every site that remains enabled throughout a tail is eventually selected on that tail. The premise is sufficient for the eventual constant record to be normal, but it is not needed for premise-free eventual constancy and is not derived or selected by canonical repair.
rows.notes: The reducible constant remoteReader flagUp control shows that arbitrary eventual constancy does not imply normality. Removal of this row needs a source theorem that produces pathwise weak fairness for the chosen adaptive scheduler; no current source theorem does so.

rows.name: work-conserving canonical adaptive choice
rows.statement: At every canonical adaptive repair state, whenever some site has an effective repair, the selected site has an effective repair. This stronger premise gives a normal and stable horizon bounded by the initial mismatch count. It is not required for premise-free eventual constancy or the weaker pathwise-fair normality theorem.
rows.notes: The alwaysProbe witness proves the premise is nonvacuous. Canonical repair supplies the available local moves but does not select a work-conserving scheduler, so the premise remains explicitly declared and is consumed only by the quantitative rank-horizon corollary.

rows.name: bounded waste between canonical adaptive changes
rows.statement: From every scheduler index and every reducible canonical repair record, at least one genuine record change occurs among the next q+1 attempts for one declared natural q. The premise permits bounded equality stutter and yields a normal horizon no larger than (q+1) times the initial mismatch count. Canonical repair does not derive q or select a scheduler.
rows.notes: Work conservation discharges the q=0 case and the committed alternating TwoCell scheduler discharges q=1. The delayed normalizing scheduler family shows that eventual normality alone does not supply any finite q or mismatch-only attempt horizon.

rows.name: sufficient cumulative attempt budget
rows.statement: The declared natural attempt budget B is at least (q+1) times the initial mismatch count for the same bounded-waste value q. Every scheduler invocation costs one unit, including equality stutter. This adequacy inequality supplies a finite execution capacity but no physical time, rate, energy, bandwidth, fee, or hardware interpretation.
rows.notes: The arbitrary-width independent-defect family proves the work-conserving q=0 threshold is worst-case sharp, while the different-patch-cardinality TwoCell source supplies a second nonisomorphic sharp instance. For general q, the registered value is a sufficient upper cap only. The number is a mathematical attempt cap only.

rows.name: certified causal read support
rows.statement: Every semantic commit declares the register versions on which its enablement, accepted payload, visible label, or continuation genuinely depends, and the declared support is sound and complete for that dependence. The generated parent relation authenticates each cited version by requiring parent write-membership, the matching writer identifier, and value continuity from the parent's post-state to the child's pre-state. The Lean execution bridge threads states but does not infer support completeness from arbitrary executor code, and a repair that does not cite the injected seam version acquires no mismatch-response edge.
rows.notes: The blind-repair control shows the citation clause is load-bearing: a repair with empty certified support repairs the seam yet acquires no injection-to-response edge. Writer labels alone are also rejected: authenticated edges require an actual parent write and exact value-version continuity. Support soundness and completeness remain receipt obligations of any producing pipeline; authentication prevents forged provenance but does not prove that the declared support includes every semantic dependency.

rows.name: abstract semantic ancestry acyclicity rank
rows.statement: An arbitrary inhabitant of the abstract SemanticEventLog certificate interface supplies a natural rank strictly increasing across every authenticated direct semantic parent edge as an acyclicity and well-foundedness witness. The canonical fresh, duplicate-free, carrier-complete executed-history constructor does not import this rank: it derives the witness from commit position and proves exact agreement with threaded authenticated provenance. The spacetime placement does not use these rank values; it computes canonical sourceHeight from authenticated parenthood. The supplied witness is not a repair schedule, modular parameter, clock reading, proper time, or global time coordinate; neither is sourceHeight.
rows.notes: The abstract rank makes the generated closure irreflexive and asymmetric, so the strict-order laws of the A1 interface are theorems rather than declarations and sourceHeight recursion is well founded. Its numerical values are not the geometry coordinate: sourceHeight is recomputed from ParentEdge as zero at roots and one plus maximum parent height. The committed chain and diamond fixtures discharge the abstract witness with event index or level rank. More importantly, semanticEventLogOfExecution removes it as an independent premise on the executed branch by deriving position rank from FreshStart, duplicate-free event identifiers, and complete finite carrier coverage. PR-82 remains registered only at the abstract certificate boundary; it must not be counted as an imported assumption of the executed-log result or as a supplied placement rank.

rows.name: pathwise weak fairness for fixed node attempts
rows.statement: Along one attempt run of an input-independent fixed node federation, if one declared node remains failing throughout a tail, that exact node is eventually selected on the tail. The premise removes reducible equality-stutter tails but does not cause accepted-step termination, select a scheduler, bound attempts, or provide a physical rate.
rows.notes: The singleton canonical scheduler proves the premise is nonvacuous. The root-only fanout scheduler proves that attempt stabilization without this premise may remain reducible. The one-member historical weak-step fixture shows fairness is insufficient when the counted relation itself permits stutter.

rows.name: bounded waste between fixed node changes
rows.statement: From every scheduler index and every non-consensus state of one input-independent fixed node federation, at least one genuine state change occurs among the next q+1 attempts for one declared natural q. Combined with the source-specific triangular potential, the premise yields stable consensus within (q+1) times the triangular node bound. It is not implied by pathwise weak fairness and gives no physical rate or unit.
rows.notes: The state-blind fixedRoundRobinScheduler discharges q = fixedProgram.length - 1 and proves the premise nonvacuous. The arbitrary-delay weak-fair family shows PR-84 does not provide a uniform finite q. Other supplied schedulers must establish their own bounded-waste witness.
